[[2012 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2012 NCAA Tournament]]}} '''Kim English''' (born September 24, 1988) is an [[United States|American]] [[college basketball]] player at the [[University of Missouri]]. ==High school career== In his senior season at [[Randallstown High School]], English averaged 18.2 points and 7.4 rebounds and was named team MVP while leading Randallstown to their third consecutive state championship.{{cite web|title=Kim English|url=http://www.mutigers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/english_kim00.html|publisher=mutigers.com|accessdate=16 March 2012}} After high school, English attended [[Notre Dame Preparatory School (Fitchburg, Massachusetts)]]. English averaged 17.3 points, 6.2 rebounds, and 3.9 assists while again earning team MVP honors. ==College recruitment== {{College Athlete Recruit Start|34=no|collapse=no|year=2008}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Kim English | position = SG | hometown = Baltimore, MD | highschool = Notre Dame | feet = 6 | inches = 5 | weight = 180 | commitdate = 9/30/2007 | scout stars = 4 | rivals stars = 3 }} |} ==College career== English committed to attend the [[University of Missouri]] on September 30, 2007.{{cite web|title=Kim English|url=http://rivals.yahoo.com/missouri/basketball/recruiting/player-Kim-English-71420;_ylt=AmvR0EiTxtt4Q7b4Nh.HQiYLs5B4|publisher=Rivals.com}} As a freshman, English worked his way into the starting lineup, starting 13 out of 16 Big 12 games. In the second round of the [[2009 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2009 NCAA Tournament]], with Mizzou tied 79-79 with [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]], English came off the bench to replace an injured [[J.T. Tiller]] and hit two free throws to give Mizzou an 81-79 lead en route to an 83-79 victory.{{cite web|title=English proves clutch; Marquette's James struggles in return|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=294000010|publisher=ESPN.com|accessdate=16 March 2012}} English averaged 14 points per game as a sophomore while earning Third Team All-Big 12 honors, becoming just the third Mizzou underclassmen to earn All-Big 12 honors, [[United States Basketball Writers Association|USBWA]] All-District honors, and being named to [[Dick Vitale]]'s All-Improved Team. As a junior English was unable to improve upon his sophomore year campaign, averaging just 10 points per game. As a senior, English averaged 14.5 points per game and made 45.9% of his three pointers, earning Third Team All-Big 12 honors for the second time.{{cite web|title=2012 Phillips 66 All-Big 12 Men's Basketball Awards Announced|url=http://www.big12sports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=10410&ATCLID=205391642|publisher=Big12Sports.com|accessdate=16 March 2012}} Leading Mizzou to its second Big 12 Tournament Championship in four years, English was named the Big 12 Tournament Most Outstanding Player after averaging 23 points and shooting 78 percent from the field.{{cite web|title=MU’s English leads Big 12 all-tournament team|url=http://www.kansascity.com/2012/03/10/3482799/mus-english-leads-big-12-all-tournament.html|publisher=Kansas City Star|accessdate=16 March 2012}} With 107 victories in four years, English, with teammates [[Marcus Denmon]] and Steve Moore won more games than any senior class in Mizzou basketball history.{{cite web|last=Paylor|first=Terez|title=Missouri seniors prepare for final game in Columbia Read more here: http://www.kansascity.com/2012/02/28/3458158/mu-seniors-prepare-for-final-home.html#storylink=cpy|url=http://www.kansascity.com/2012/02/28/3458158/mu-seniors-prepare-for-final-home.html|publisher=Kansas City Star|accessdate=16 March 2012}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[http://www.mutigers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/english_kim00.html Missouri Tigers Bio] {{Persondata | NAME = English, Kim | ALTERNATIVE NAMES = | SHORT DESCRIPTION = Basketball player | DATE OF BIRTH = 24 September 1988 | PLACE OF BIRTH = | DATE OF DEATH = | PLACE OF DEATH = }} {{DEFAULTSORT:English, Kim}} [[Category:1988 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Basketball players from Maryland]] [[Category:Missouri Tigers men's basketball players]] [[Category:Shooting guards]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Baltimore, Maryland]]
